about.title: Tracy Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product you trusted failed, and now you're dealing with the fallout in Tracy. Maybe a space heater caught fire in a home off 11th Street, a tire blew apart on I-205 during the afternoon commute, or a power tool guard gave way in a garage near Corral Hollow Road. Whatever the item, California treats these cases differently from ordinary negligence claims. Under strict product liability, you usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Tracy sits in San Joaquin County, and the same rule applies whether the product was bought at a local store, ordered online, or came installed in a vehicle. Responsibility can reach the maker, the distributor, and the retailer. We handle product liability claims on a contingency basis—no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Strict Liability Is Explained Up Front
items.desc: We understand that in California you generally need to show a design, manufacturing, or warning defect caused your injury, not that anyone was negligent. That distinction shapes how your claim is built from day one.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Comes First
items.desc: The product itself is often the single most important piece of proof. We can help you secure the item, its packaging, receipts, and any photos before anything is discarded or repaired.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Is Considered
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may each bear responsibility under California law. We identify all of them rather than stopping at the first name on the box.

items.question: A part on my car failed while I was driving on I-205 near Tracy. Is that a car accident case or a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be both, and the difference matters. Tracy recorded 221 injury collisions in 2025, and a portion of crashes anywhere involve failed brakes, tires, airbags, or steering components rather than driver error alone. If a defect contributed, you may have a strict liability claim against the manufacturer in addition to any claim against another driver. We can review the vehicle and repair records to sort that out.

items.question: Do I really need to keep the broken product?
items.answer: Yes, as much as you safely can. In a strict liability case the product is the evidence, and once it is thrown out or fixed, proving the defect becomes far harder. Keep the item, its packaging, manuals, and receipts, and photograph everything before moving it. If the product is hazardous, let us know rather than disposing of it yourself.

items.question: I bought the product online, not from a store in Tracy. Who is responsible?
items.answer: Where you bought it usually does not change your rights under California law. The manufacturer, the distributor, and the seller can all be held liable for a defective product, whether it arrived by delivery truck or came from a shelf on Grant Line Road. We can trace the supply chain to identify each party. There is no fee unless there is a recovery.
